quarterly_data.signal: Dominion Energy 2026 IRP Update - large-load requests: as of February 2026 the company had received approximately 25,000 megawatts of large-load delivery point requests with projected connection dates through December 31, 2031, and those requests continue to grow. The company builds its data center billing demand forecast from seven customer-specific segments (the seven largest and/or fastest growing data center customers) plus an eighth segment combining all other data center customers (approximately 47).

quarterly_data.quarter: Dominion Energy regulatory filing: 2026 Integrated Resource Plan Update (10-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Dominion Energy 2026 IRP Update - load forecast: under the 2026 PJM Derived Load Forecast used for all portfolios, the DOM Zone coincident peak grows at a 20-year CAGR of 4.2% (DOM LSE 2.8%, Residual DOM Zone 6.7%) and annual energy at 5.2% (DOM LSE 3.8%, Residual DOM Zone 7.5%); DOM Zone winter and summer non-coincident peaks are projected to grow 3.9% and 4.1% a year. PJM's DOM Zone forecast rose in the out years for the fifth year in a row, with changes in the data center load forecast a key driver. The company says the PJM Derived non-coincident peak forecast starts approximately 500 MW below the 2025 DOM LSE historical peak and that a potentially downward biased forecast could mask reliability risks.
quarterly_data.figure: DOM Zone coincident peak 20-year CAGR 4.2% (DOM LSE 2.8%, Residual 6.7%); energy 5.2% (3.8%, 7.5%); winter / summer peaks 3.9% / 4.1% CAGR; PJM Derived peak approximately 500 MW below 2025 historical peak

quarterly_data.quarter: Dominion Energy regulatory filing: 2026 Integrated Resource Plan Update (10-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Dominion Energy 2026 IRP Update - Company Preferred Plan (PJM Derived Load Forecast, 20-year planning period): 39.2 GW of new resources with a total plan cost of $183.4 billion and $91.5 billion of construction capex - 21,229 MW of solar, 3,479 MW of wind, 3,525 MW of storage, 8,965 MW of natural gas and 2,046 MW of nuclear, including three sets of SMRs starting in 2042 and 3.4 GW of additional offshore wind. The plan would require the company to seek the VCEA reliability exception to preserve existing generation and add 8.9 GW of gas-fired assets. The company says natural gas generation will remain a critical component of its strategy to meet the load forecast absent a commercially viable carbon-free dispatchable alternative.
quarterly_data.figure: 39.2 GW new resources; $183.4 billion total plan cost; $91.5 billion construction capex; 8,965 MW gas, 21,229 MW solar, 3,479 MW wind, 3,525 MW storage, 2,046 MW nuclear

quarterly_data.quarter: Dominion Energy regulatory filing: 2026 Integrated Resource Plan Update (10-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Dominion Energy 2026 IRP Update - data center load sensitivities: a high load forecast scaled to the company's internal 95th percentile data center forecast (with half the forecast energy-efficiency savings) starts 3% above the PJM Derived Load Forecast and reaches 14% higher by 2040, requiring 44,197 MW of additions at a $217.0 billion portfolio cost; the low case (5th percentile data center forecast) starts 2% lower and reaches 13% lower by 2040 (36,359 MW, $155.4 billion). A Virginia Staff-directed case limiting data center growth to customers with completed electric service agreements is approximately $25 billion less expensive, but the company says it does not represent a future where it meets its obligation to serve and does not consider it a feasible path.
quarterly_data.figure: high load: +3% first year to +14% by 2040, 44,197 MW, $217.0 billion; low load: -2% to -13% by 2040, 36,359 MW, $155.4 billion

quarterly_data.quarter: Dominion Energy regulatory filing: 2026 Integrated Resource Plan Update (10-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Dominion Energy 2026 IRP Update - large-load tariff: the SCC-approved GS-5 customer class covers customers with contracted or measured demand of 25 megawatts or more and a load factor of 75% or more, taking service under GS-5 from January 1, 2027 (not exclusive to data centers); high-load customers face minimum demand charges, a 14-year contract term, exit fees equal to the minimum demand charges over the unexpired term, and collateral requirements (e.g., $1.5 million/MW, reducible based on established credit). On September 4, 2026 the company proposed a new customer class and high load tariff in North Carolina with minimum demand obligations, a 14-year contract term, collateral requirements and limits on capacity reductions.
quarterly_data.figure: GS-5: 25 megawatts or more and 75% load factor; from January 1, 2027; collateral e.g. $1.5 million/MW; 14-year contract; North Carolina proposal September 4, 2026

quarterly_data.quarter: Dominion Energy regulatory filing: 2026 Integrated Resource Plan Update (10-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Dominion Energy 2026 IRP Update - SMRs: the company furthered its assessment of SMR siting at the North Anna Power Station, received SCC approval in July 2026 of its second Rider SMR application (recovery of eligible early-stage development costs), and is evaluating financing approaches and commercial structures including arrangements with third parties and large-load customers; depending on those evaluations, SMR deployment could occur earlier than assumed in the IRP portfolios.
